text:
maria: FYI bringing up eu-north2 GPU cluster for Q2 capacity. Hit a blocker during node bootstrap — gpu-nodes-003 stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. Logs show driver mount errors and CNI flapping. Can someone take a look?

aj: on it. which AMI and bootstrap script version?

maria: ami-0a1b2c3d (gpu-optimized-v2), bootstrap v2026-03-17. terraform apply succeeded, then kubelet started and died.

harry: can you paste the kubelet/journalctl snippet? also any kernel module install failures?

maria: snippet:
```
Mar 17 12:03:02 gpu-nodes-003 kubelet[2312]: E0320 12:03:02.123456 2312 kubelet.go:234] Failed to start container "nvidia-device-plugin": failed to mount "/dev/nvidia0": no such file or directory
Mar 17 12:03:02 gpu-nodes-003 cloud-init[1450]: install-nvidia-driver.sh: exit 2
```

lina: that exit code usually means the driver packaging step hit the kernel version check. We saw a similar pattern when the AMI kernel was rolled to 6.x earlier than our DKMS build expects.

aj: checking bootstrap logs from s3: `/bootstrap/logs/gpu-nodes-003/` — yep the driver installer log shows `incompatible kernel headers`. The transient workaround is to skip DKMS and install vendor binary, but that changes immutable AMI expectations.

maria: we just kicked off an automated rollback for gpu-nodepool because several nodes failed health checks — deploy-bot reported: 
`deploy-bot: rollback triggered for module:gpu-node-pool (reason: >3 node failures)`

harry: noted. before we re-run we should validate the AMI/kernel combo and the node bootstrap order. Also saw CNI `calico` flapping due to MTU mismatch after adding ENI trunking. Could be two independent failures colliding.

lina: +1 — MTU mismatch shows routes bouncing: `flannel0` down/up, then calicoctl shows BGP peer reset. If kube-proxy restarts during that window the node looks unhealthy and autoscaler kills it.

aj: action items: 1) pin AMI to gpu-optimized-v1 with known-good kernel for this rollout, 2) patch bootstrap to verify kernel headers before DKMS step and fallback to vendor installer, 3) add a preflight check for MTU on primary ENI. I'm going to open a tiny runbook PR with checks.

maria: thanks. do we want to hold capacity admission (no new nodepool rollouts) until this is fixed? cost concerns if we keep retrying autoscale.

harry: recommend pause. i've set a short-term policy: no auto-rollout for new gpu nodepools in eu-north2 until signoff. That should limit churn and cost.

sre-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-0427 — eu-north2 gpu bootstrap failures (triggered by maria). Assigned: aj, harry.

aj: i'm running a repro with the problematic AMI in a staging VPC. if reproduce, i'll create a hotfix ami + validation tests and post here. ETA 2 hours.

maria: sounds good. if aj needs extra hands for the AMI rebuild let me know. i'll coordinate with infra-alloc to hold capacity budget. :thumbsup:

harry: extra tip — add a `sleep 30` after nvme attach in bootstrap; we saw race where NVMe device nodes appear a few seconds after driver install and kubelet starts too quickly. might reduce flake while AMI gets rebuilt.

lina: logging capture suggestion: add `kubectl describe node` + `journalctl -u kubelet --since "15m"` to bootstrap error email to S3 so we have triage artifacts.

maria: copying action items: pin AMI -> aj, fallback driver install + preflight -> aj, MTU check -> lina, pause rollouts -> harry, logging capture -> maria. will update runbook PR once fixes are validated.

deploy-bot: terraform plan approved (no changes to nodepool while pause tag is active).

aj: quick update — reproduced driver header failure in staging. building hotfix AMI now. will attach logs and PR link in ~90m.

maria: thanks everyone, keeping this thread as the single source for the bring-up blocker.

harry: once hotfix AMI is validated we should run a small canary (2 nodes) and monitor: kubelet stability, device-plugin readiness, CNI BGP adjacency for 10m before scaling.

lina: noted — i'll extend canary monitoring dashboards and add token-level cost estimate so we can see churn impact.

sre-bot: INC-2026-0427 status: mitigated -> monitoring. last_message_ts=1793457100
